subject: Request: fence-and-bridge network narrative + diagrams for SIG review
messages:
From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@blueriversec.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: fence-and-bridge network narrative + diagrams for SIG review

Hi Kimberly —

We're kicking off the SIG questionnaire review and the control owners asked for a short network narrative that explains Redwood's approach to tenant fencing and selective bridging for Dedicated/Private deployments. Specifically we're looking for:

- A short one-page narrative describing the "fence" (tenant isolation) and the "bridge" (controlled shared services/ingress) concepts in Redwood's architecture.
- A topology diagram that highlights control-plane vs data-plane boundaries, egress controls, and where KV-caches and model artifacts live for Dedicated vs Private deployments.
- A control mapping (who owns it, enforcement mechanism, evidence pointers).

Can you provide a draft by EOD today? If not, an initial package (diagram + bullets) tomorrow morning would be fine.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn.

Sam Chen
Senior Auditor
BlueRiver Security

Attachment: none

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sam Chen <sam.chen@blueriversec.com>
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: fence-and-bridge network narrative + diagrams for SIG review

Sam —

Thanks for the clear ask. Rafael and I will assemble a focused package that uses the "fence & bridge" terminology so it matches your reviewers' expectations. Quick plan:

1) I will draft a 1-page narrative that explains the concepts and the rationale for selective bridging (shared services that must cross tenant boundaries with controls).
2) Rafael will produce a topology PNG that annotates control-plane vs data-plane, egress ACLs, and where model artifacts/KV caches are stored for both Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated GPU pools) and Private (customer VPC/on-prem).
3) We'll include a 1-page control matrix mapping SIG controls to our implementation and evidence links.

We can get a first pass to you by 15:30 PT today. If BlueRiver needs a longer walkthrough, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow.

Avery — looping you in for any product nuance around shared services.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none (diagram will follow)

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Sam Chen <sam.chen@blueriversec.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: fence-and-bridge network narrative + diagrams for SIG review

On Mon, Apr 11, 2027 at 10:22 AM Sam Chen <sam.chen@blueriversec.com> wrote:
> We're kicking off the SIG questionnaire review and the control owners asked for a short network narrative that explains Redwood's approach to tenant fencing and selective bridging for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Thanks, Sam — attaching the first-pass assets. Key highlights below, followed by attachments.

Summary bullets (TL;DR):
- "Fence": Each tenant runs in logically segmented runtime pools. For Dedicated customers that means reserved GPU pools in isolated VPCs with per-tenant routing; for Private (VPC/on-prem) the tenant owns the network boundary.
- "Bridge": Shared services (model artifact repository, telemetry, license metering) are reachable via tightly scoped, authenticated bridges implemented with mutual TLS, IP allowlists, and per-tenant ACLs. Bridges are one-way where possible (ingress-only) and audited.
- Control-plane is isolated: customer control-plane operations (rollouts, model versioning) use a separate management VPC and authenticated API endpoints with role-based access; no customer data plane traffic traverses the control-plane in Private deployments.
- KV cache and model artifacts: KV caches live on the serving nodes and are ephemeral per-tenant; persistent model artifacts are hosted in our artifact storage with encryption-at-rest and strict access policies. Dedicated pools may host cached artifacts locally to reduce egress but are still access-controlled.

Attachments in this message:
- fence-bridge-topology-v1.png (annotated topology, highlights egress, control-plane boundary, bridge services)
- control-matrix-20270411.pdf (one-page mapping of SIG/CIS controls -> implementation + evidence links)

Notes on evidence pointers (see control matrix):
- Mutual TLS cert chain for bridges: internal CA + documented rotation cadence (link in PDF).
- Egress monitoring: VPC flow logs + Cloud-native egress DLP hooks for hosted customers; for Private we provide guidance and optional agent.
- Audit trails: API call logs, model rollout records, DSAR logs retained per policy.

If you'd like, I can annotate a second variant of the topology that shows an air-gapped on-prem deployment for SIG reviewers who ask specifically about offline options.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: fence-bridge-topology-v1.png; control-matrix-20270411.pdf

From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@blueriversec.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: fence-and-bridge network narrative + diagrams for SIG review

Kimberly / Rafael —

Received the package, thank you. Quick notes from an initial pass:

- Topology looks good; reviewers asked for a small inset that explicitly shows the mTLS handshake flow for "bridge" connections (client cert, API gateway, service cert). Could you add that into the diagram as a 2nd slide?
- In the narrative, please add one sentence that clarifies that Dedicated GPU pools may be single-tenant at the network layer (VPC) and that Redwood's runtime still enforces per-tenant KV separation at process/scheduler boundaries.
- For evidence, the review team prefers a short URL per control (rather than a long Drive folder link) when possible — the control matrix had a couple of long pointers. Could you add canonical short links (we can accept HubSpot or a signed drive link).

If you can add the inset + short links by EOD tomorrow we'll be in good shape for the SIG review kickoff. Otherwise we'll propose a follow-up slot.

I'll book a 20-minute sync if we need to walk through annotations.

Best,
Sam
Senior Auditor
BlueRiver Security
thread_summary: BlueRiver Security requested a concise 'fence & bridge' deliverable for SIG review. Redwood's compliance team (Kimberly) and Security Architect (Rafael) responded with a one-page narrative, annotated topology, and a control matrix; auditor asked for a small mTLS handshake inset and short evidence links for final submission.
